answer: Agents can make a new identity useful only by earning signed attestations from established peers. A newcomer must complete randomly assigned trades and lock collateral, while peers cross-check its behavior through a bridge and slash the stake when it forks histories or colludes. A whisper from one account therefore cannot bootstrap a fleet: the attacker must finance many deposits, sustain observable activity, and lose collateral when identities are exposed, making a glacier of fake agents expensive.
